# AGENTS.md

Spec-driven development kit. Work moves through a fixed chain of artifacts, and every stage reads the one before it rather than re-deriving intent from the original request.

## The chain

```
requirements.md  ->  design.md  ->  tasks.json  ->  [human gate]  ->  dev agents
```

Artifacts live in `docs/features/<slug>/`. Repository context lives in `.agentteam/repo-map.md` and `.agentteam/company.md`.

## Skills

| Skill | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `architect-design` | Turn an approved-or-draft requirements.md into a technical design — components, data model, interfaces, and the architect's share of the batched open questions. |
| `dev-task-split` | Split an approved design.md into an ordered list of dev tasks with explicit file ownership, so the orchestrator knows which tasks are safe to run in parallel and which must run in sequence. |
| `pm-requirements` | Turn a short feature request into a requirements document with use cases, edge cases, testable acceptance criteria, and one batched list of open questions. |
| `qa-test-plan` | Turn an approved requirements.md into a failing test suite, one test per acceptance criterion, so dev agents get an objective pass/fail exit condition instead of a prose bug report to reinterpret. |
| `repo-indexer` | Read an existing repository and produce the agent context files — repo-map.md and a draft company.md — that every other agent depends on. |

Each skill's full instructions are in `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, mirrored as Cursor commands in `.cursor/commands/`.

## House rules

- **Never widen a task past its `owns` globs.** Tasks run concurrently in separate worktrees; files outside your globs belong to another agent and your edits to them will be discarded at merge time.
- **Tests are the exit condition**, not your own judgement that the code looks right. A bug is filed as a failing test, never as prose.
- **Open questions are batched.** Add them to the numbered `Qn` list in the current artifact rather than asking one at a time.
- **Never put credentials, connection strings or customer data** in `.agentteam/` files — they are committed and read straight into prompts.

## Commands

```console
python3 -m orchestrator validate docs/features/<slug>/tasks.json
python3 -m orchestrator schedule docs/features/<slug>/tasks.json
python3 -m orchestrator run      docs/features/<slug>/tasks.json
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests
```
